label: Kiro CLI
description: One conversation with Kiro CLI, AWS's coding agent, the successor of Amazon Q Developer CLI: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, Kiro CLI runs on your machine (a local install only) from your own install of `kiro-cli` with your own login, working in `folder`. If `kiro-cli` is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own, shared by the whole machine, before the node runs. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. It runs only on Kiro's own models, billed in your account's credits; the title it would ask a model for on every new conversation is off. A refusal can carry your note, which its model reads. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission mode, the model, the reasoning effort and extra folders. Your program's tools reach Kiro's model as `weft::<tool>`, which it loads with its `tool_load` when it needs one, and come back to your program under their plain names. Kiro CLI cannot let a program's tool take one of its own tools' places, so a tool named like one of them (`read_file`, `execute_bash`, `web_fetch` and the rest of this node's list) is refused when the program is built.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run Kiro CLI in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A KiroCliAccess's `access`: a Kiro API key. Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, Kiro CLI uses the login already on it (`kiro-cli login`).

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder Kiro CLI works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the Kiro CLI program to run, when it is not the `kiro-cli` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What Kiro CLI may do without asking. `ask`: every request it would put to a person comes out of AskAgent as a question. `accept_edits`: edits in the folder go ahead, the rest asks. `plan`: it only plans. `bypass`: nothing asks, nothing is refused; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: A model id Kiro offers your account, such as `claude-sonnet-4.5` (https://kiro.dev/docs/models/). Left out, Kiro's default.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Reasoning effort
inputs.description: How hard the model reasons: one of the levels the chosen model offers, which a model with none ignores.

inputs.name: addDirs
inputs.label: Extra folders
inputs.description: Folders besides `folder` Kiro CLI may read and change.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: KiroCli '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
KiroCli '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a KiroCliAccess on `access`.
KiroCli '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
KiroCli '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, accept_edits, plan, bypass.
KiroCli '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
KiroCli '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs Kiro CLI itself.
